annotationRationale: The main task is constructing sufficient states for recursive path counting. Both methods use the finite adjacency model and probabilities from equally likely directions; the alternative replaces recursion with disjoint first-exit cases.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is correct; no repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: Independent counting gives 936 safe direction sequences out of 7776, hence 13/108, choice A. The stem and key are consistent. The reference diagram's “2+ away” state should mean that an exit has occurred: an outward endpoint can be only sqrt(3) units away. Both candidates correctly use distance greater than 1.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: No shared-bank methods are supplied. LIVE and AMC Mastery Solutions 1 through 4 use equivalent state recursions, represented by the first method. AMC Mastery Solution 6 supplies the retained first-exit alternative. Solution 5 enumerates successful state patterns; another such enumeration would add little to these two complete routes.
review.annotationCheck: State recursion is appropriately assessed, with graph modeling and classical probability supporting it. The alternative's multiplication, disjoint addition, and complement concepts are correctly attached locally. No contextual role is needed.
review.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is correct; no repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The seven permitted vertices have the stated adjacencies. The transition (a,b) to (b,6a+2b) counts every safe extension exactly once. Every table row checks, ending at (192,744), so the probability is 936/6^5=13/108. Convexity of the disk also verifies the restriction during each move.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Accurately credits the nonofficial LIVE recurrence and AMC Mastery Solution 1 as source-informed-original. The expanded recurrence justification, table, and continuous-distance observation provide an independently developed explanation.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The endpoint grouping is motivated, b_n explicitly combines all six surrounding endpoints, and both recurrence coefficients are explained. The table is fully reconstructible.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: All three IDs fit: sufficient-state counting, finite adjacency paths, and favorable outcomes divided by equally likely outcomes are explicitly used.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact 古典概型 link matches the final uniform sample-space calculation. The graph and state-recursion nodes have no supplied CN links, which is an honest competition-skill gap.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: 7.SP.C.8a supports the favorable-outcome fraction. S-CP.B.9 is only adjacent because no permutation or combination calculation is required. No supplied US link covers the state-recursion construction.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The recursive-counting node captures the decisive modeling step precisely; graph-models and cnm_h137 correctly support it.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The transition probabilities 1/6, 1/3, and 1/2 are correct at every surrounding vertex. First exits on moves 2 through 5 have respectively 1, 1, 2, and 3 possible state prefixes. Every listed product checks, and their disjoint total is 95/108. Taking the complement gives 13/108.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Faithfully credits AMC Mastery Solution 6 without claiming official status. It makes the first-exit interpretation precise and avoids the source's misleading suggestion that every outward move reaches distance 2.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The first-exit partition, prefix products, exhaustiveness restrictions, and complement are explained sufficiently. Stopping each pattern at X correctly includes every later continuation.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: Graph modeling, uniform direction probabilities, conditional multiplication, disjoint addition, and complementary events all appear directly. A recursion node is appropriately absent.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact classical-probability, addition, and complementary-event links fit. The partial multiplication-rule link supports these positive-probability conditional products. Graph modeling has no supplied CN alignment.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: S-CP.B.8 supports the ordered conditional products in the uniform direction model; S-CP.B.7 is used in its disjoint special case. 7.SP.C.8a supports the elementary fractions. No supplied US link directly covers the complement node.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: All five IDs match concrete steps. The method uses first-exit casework rather than an unexplained Markov-chain theorem.
